skipped.PT090: Duplicate of PT002 — same 'three blockhead sons' frame (King Immortal-Power, Maidens' Delight), only the sons' names differ and they are borrowed from other stories. Titled 'front matter'; looks like a mislabelled extra record. Confirm and delete from the corpus rather than tag.

notes: skills priors are ORDINAL 0-3 proposals for human review; they are never summed
calibration is engine-written; empty here by design
skills is a flat block when both bands agree; use a per-band dict when they differ
attention_load is a demand parameter, not a mastered skill (see PRODUCT_RESEARCH.md §2)
draft_unreviewed counts entries still marked _draft in data/story_tags_authored.json

age_map.rationale: No violence or death anywhere; the only heavy content is abstract talk of twelve years of grammar and a hundred land-grants, which keeps it at 5+ rather than 4.

moral.text: The right guidance at the right time can turn a fool wise

video_brief.key_beat: Vishnusharman standing before King Immortal-Power, boldly promising to make the three dull princes wise within six months.

age_map.rationale: A 4-9 band exists and no death occurs on the page (Lively survives), but the servants' false report of his death and the jackals' jealous plot to be rid of him are the whole engine, so 5+.

moral.text: Jealousy and lies destroy friendship

video_brief.key_beat: Cheek and Victor the jackals huddled together under the banyan tree, whispering their plot against the strong bull Lively.

age_map.rationale: Only the 9+ band exists. The curious monkey is hurt when the beam falls and is lectured by Victor; the harm is non-fatal in this telling.

moral.text: Think before you act, or carelessness will hurt you

video_brief.key_beat: The monkey tugging the wedge out of the half-built temple beam, the timber crashing down on him.

age_map.rationale: no harm; the 'scary noise' reveal is gentle

moral.text: Don't judge something by its noise or appearance.

video_brief.key_beat: the jackal gnawing into the drum

age_map.rationale: A jealous servant falsely accuses the good merchant Strong-Tooth of kissing the queen and the king withdraws his favor; no violence but adult themes of sexual slander and court intrigue in the only (9+) band.

moral.text: A small word from a small man can raise or ruin a reputation

video_brief.key_beat: Bull pointing a finger at Strong-Tooth beside the sleeping king's bed as the king's face hardens.

age_map.rationale: The 4-9 text softens the murder to a straight theft, but it keeps June's explicit thought of killing Godly for the treasure, plus calculated seduction of a holy man's trust.

moral.text: A predator will wear friendship like a mask to reach what he wants

video_brief.key_beat: June bowing low at Godly's feet with folded hands while his eyes slide sideways toward the treasure under the old man's arm.

age_map.rationale: nested frame (jackal fable inside the June betrayal) needs tracking; both deaths are off-page

moral.text: Greed and foolishness lead to trouble.

video_brief.key_beat: the jackal caught between the two rams

stories.title: How the Crow-Hen Killed the Black Snake

age_map.rationale: The black snake devours the crow's newborn chicks and the snake itself dies choking on a fish bone (a crab strangles the heron's greed in the 9+ nested tale) - deaths of young and old, though told gently.

moral.text: Cruelty and greed eventually destroy the one who practices them

video_brief.key_beat: The black snake rearing back, a sharp fish bone jammed in its throat as it thrashes against the banyan trunk.

age_map.rationale: tyrant is tricked to drown; the 'is it fair to trick him?' tension is the point

moral.text: Cleverness beats strength.

video_brief.key_beat: Numskull roaring at his own reflection in the well

stories.title: The Weaver Who Loved a Princess

age_map.rationale: Only the 9+ band exists. A deception romance - a weaver poses as the god Vishnu to marry a princess - climaxes in a war where the god's discus cuts King Valor in two; impersonating a deity plus an on-page death keep it out of the younger band.

moral.text: The gods befriend the man who climbs the height of determination.

video_brief.key_beat: The weaver disguised as the god Vishnu, riding the carved wooden Garuda, descending onto the princess's moonlit balcony.

age_map.rationale: The Brahman is punished for a rescued man's ingratitude - the king orders him impaled and the snake poisons the queen to force his release; rescues from a well plus arrest, poisoning and reversal, only in the 9+ band.

moral.text: Gratitude is a virtue and ingratitude brings its own ruin

video_brief.key_beat: The Brahman peering down into the grassy well where a tiger, monkey, snake and man tilt their faces up at him.

age_map.rationale: the kind host is punished for the guest's fault — a real fairness question for M4/M5

moral.text: Don't invite strangers to stay in your home.

video_brief.key_beat: Leap biting the king's back

age_map.rationale: CURATION OVERRULE: curation verdict is NINE_PLUS on the frame's misogynist verse, not the fable (HANDOVER §5). Adapted text shows no blood; the death is one line.

moral.text: Whoever betrays his true nature will eventually be discovered and punished.

video_brief.key_beat: the pack of jackals howling, betraying his true nature

age_map.rationale: The sleeping swan Passion is shot dead by a caravan archer who misreads the owl's hoot as an omen - an on-page killing, though the 4-9 text tells it without gore.

moral.text: A stray word or sudden act can kill - even between friends

video_brief.key_beat: The archer drawing his bow on the dozing swan as the owl's hoot echoes over the lake at dawn.

age_map.rationale: The jackal and crow scheme to have the camel Ugly killed to feed the sick lion; Ugly volunteers and his body is torn apart and devoured - on-page cannibalism, 9+ band only.

moral.text: Those who live by their wits are devoured by their own cleverness

video_brief.key_beat: The starving lion, jackal, crow and leopard ringed around Ugly as he bows low and offers his own life.

age_map.rationale: The lion's jackal and crow companions secretly plan to kill the carpenter and seize his food, and only a 9+ text exists - though the told version ends with the friendship intact and no death.

moral.text: You are judged by the company you keep

video_brief.key_beat: The carpenter and his wife up in the branches glaring down at the lion flanked by a grinning jackal and crow.

stories.title: The Plover Who Fought the Ocean

age_map.rationale: No violence or death anywhere - a boastful plover and his clear-eyed wife argue over whether the tide will reach their nest, safe for the youngest band.

moral.text: Know your own limits and listen to friendly advice before you act

video_brief.key_beat: Sprawl puffing out his chest on the sand and shouting at the incoming waves while Constance watches, unimpressed.

age_map.rationale: 4-9 text says 'cut him up with knives' — the only graphic line; fine 7+, soften for 4-6

moral.text: Always listen carefully to good advice.

video_brief.key_beat: Shell-Neck opening his mouth to speak mid-flight

age_map.rationale: Fatalist is caught in the net and beaten to death with clubs, so the story carries a real killing despite the gentle 4-9 telling. (The 9+ telling no longer carries the plover nested frame — see scripts/fix_pt022_graft.py.)

moral.text: Plan ahead before danger arrives, or pay for your delay.

video_brief.key_beat: The fishermen's net sweeping up the whole lake, Fatalist thrashing in the mesh while Readywit lies still.

stories.title: The Duel between Elephant and Sparrow

age_map.rationale: The woodpecker pecks out the elephant's eyes and the blinded elephant topples into a pit and dies, and the sparrows' eggs are crushed, so it is a revenge killing despite the animal cast.

moral.text: Even the strongest can be brought down by many small allies working one clever plan.

video_brief.key_beat: The blinded elephant stumbling after the frog's croak and plunging into the deep pit.

age_map.rationale: No character is killed or eaten; the geese are snared but escape by playing dead, so the story is servable young with only mild trap peril.

moral.text: Heed the warning of the old and wise before the danger grows.

video_brief.key_beat: The geese lying still as the hunter frees and hurls them down, then bursting up together in flight.

age_map.rationale: The lion misjudges the ram and kills him in a swift pounce, so a death is present even though the 4-9 telling softens it.

moral.text: Do not judge another's strength by the surface you see.

video_brief.key_beat: The lion springing on the peacefully grazing ram.

age_map.rationale: Smart tricks the camel into being killed and eaten, then frames the wolf and drives the lion off with a Death-God lie; the 9+ band adds a 100-percent-interest bargain and a Death-God guarantee.

moral.text: One who uses cleverness to harm others is finally undone by it.

video_brief.key_beat: Smart licking his chops in the empty forest as the lion flees from the imagined Death-God.

stories.title: The Monk Who Left His Body Behind

age_map.rationale: The monk is locked in his cell and his body is burned to expose the heaven-travel lie, a burning that reads as violent even though the trickster is only pretending.

moral.text: A confident liar can fool even the mighty, but only until someone checks.

video_brief.key_beat: The locked cell going up in flames with the naked monk still inside.

stories.title: The Girl Who Married a Snake

age_map.rationale: No death or violence occurs; the complexity is courtship and a bride who insists on marrying a snake, which suits older children rather than preschoolers.

moral.text: Stand by your promise and accept what is destined for you.

video_brief.key_beat: The bride calmly declaring she will marry the snake as her relatives recoil in horror.

age_map.rationale: The parrot Blossom dies at the mere sight of Death, and the tale turns on abstract fate and death-gods that young children cannot follow.

moral.text: Some things happen simply because they are fated, and no one can prevent them.

video_brief.key_beat: Blossom dropping dead on Indra's hand the instant Death appears.

age_map.rationale: Even the softened 4-9 band has Red-Face grab the bird Needle-Face and throw her on a rock so she dies, and the 9+ band makes the death explicit; a killing keeps this above 4-5.

moral.text: Blind stubbornness that ignores good advice can bring real harm

video_brief.key_beat: Red-Face seizing Needle-Face and hurling her onto the rock

age_map.rationale: No death in either band, but the 4-9 text still carries theft, a friend framing a friend, a court ordeal, and a father asked to lie as a false witness, which is dense for the very young.

moral.text: Trusting a dishonest friend's clever scheme leads only to ruin

video_brief.key_beat: The two men digging in the ground and finding the buried pot of dinars gone

stories.title: A Remedy Worse than the Disease

age_map.rationale: Flagged murder x1; the snake eats the heron babies before they can fly and the mungoose kills the snake then eats all the herons, present even in the 4-9 band.

moral.text: A remedy chosen in panic can be worse than the disease it cures

video_brief.key_beat: The mungoose charging up the fig tree after the trail of fish bits and killing the snake

age_map.rationale: a child is kidnapped to force a confession — slapstick in telling, but the plot beat is heavy; honesty-vs-cunning is a real dilemma (M5)

moral.text: Honesty is always the best choice.

video_brief.key_beat: Naduk producing the 'hawk carried him off' excuse

age_map.rationale: Flagged murder x1 but no one actually dies in either band; the only violent content is the caged parrot shouting Bind the king, kill him, plus the capture of the chicks and a horse running off.

moral.text: The company we keep and the lessons we learn shape who we become

video_brief.key_beat: The caged parrot screeching Bind him, kill him at the king as he passes

age_map.rationale: No death occurs, but the chief repeatedly threatens to cut the travelers' stomachs open and the thief volunteers his own stomach to be cut first — in-text mutilation, floored at 7 to match the corpus's graphic-violence tier (PT023 blinding, PT027 burning) rather than the fable-death floor of 6.

moral.text: A sensible enemy can be a better friend than a selfish ally

video_brief.key_beat: The thief stepping forward and asking the chief to cut open his stomach first

age_map.rationale: Only the 9+ band exists (flagged misogyny x1; murder x5): the sword-bearer monkey strikes at a bee and kills the king outright, so no 4-9 text exists to serve.

moral.text: Keep your distance from fools, for their help can destroy you

video_brief.key_beat: The monkey swinging its sword at the bee and striking the king dead

age_map.rationale: Only the 9+ band exists (flagged cannibal x1; murder x1); the hunter arrives with a snare and club and bloodshot eyes to trap the doves, so min_age must be at least 9.

moral.text: United action and teamwork overcome even the greatest obstacles

video_brief.key_beat: The hundred doves rising as one flock and carrying the whole snare away into the sky

age_map.rationale: Flagged murder x1; even the softened 4-9 band has the second neck eating poison and both necks dying because they share one belly, so a death rules out the 4-5 tier.

moral.text: Greed and selfishness destroy even those who share one fate

video_brief.key_beat: The two necks of the single Bharunda bird pulling apart, one reaching for nectar and the other for poison

age_map.rationale: No violence in either band - just a guest briefly offended by a distracted host and a food-stealing mouse - and the 4-9 text is plain dialogue.

moral.text: Listen past a friend's odd behaviour to find the real trouble behind it

video_brief.key_beat: Crop-Ear absently whacking the alms-bowl with a bamboo stick while Wide-Bottom tries to talk to him.

age_map.rationale: No violence, but the whole story is an adult marital quarrel over poverty and charity laced with quoted sayings, so the abstract dialogue sits above the preschool band.

moral.text: Even a small gift given at the right time brings great reward

video_brief.key_beat: The Brahman gesturing up at the rain-cloud that gives only water yet is honoured by the whole world.

age_map.rationale: Three deaths - the boar gores the hunter through the stomach, the boar dies of its wound, and the jackal is impaled through the mouth by the snapping bow-tip.

moral.text: Greed devours the greedy, however clever the plan

video_brief.key_beat: The bow-tip snapping free and driving up into the jackal's mouth as he gnaws the bowstring.

age_map.rationale: Night-time trysts, a princess inviting a prince to her room, a policeman slipping off to meet a woman, and a daughter who marries a stranger in the dark - romantic and adulterous intrigue only fit for 9+.

moral.text: What is truly yours will reach you, however accidental the path looks

video_brief.key_beat: Mister Duly grabbing the rampaging elephant's trunk and hauling the bride clear of the stampeding procession.

age_map.rationale: Soft twice loses his savings and then tries to hang himself from the banyan tree - a bloodless but real suicide attempt that rules out the younger band.

moral.text: Wealth you can neither enjoy nor share is worth almost nothing

video_brief.key_beat: The rope pulled taut on the banyan branch as the glowing figure appears in the sky to stop Soft.

age_map.rationale: Both bands dwell on the bull's hanging testicles as the prize the jackals stalk for fifteen years - anatomy-driven humour aimed well past the preschool band.

moral.text: Do not let another's goading drag you away from what is sensible

video_brief.key_beat: The two jackals crouched in the grass, eyes fixed on Hang-Ball's swaying hindquarters as he drinks at the river.

stories.title: The Mice That Set Elephants Free

age_map.rationale: gentlest of the pilot; no death, reciprocal-help theme is explicit

moral.text: Make friends with everyone, big or small.

video_brief.key_beat: the mice gnawing through the elephant-snare ropes

age_map.rationale: No deaths in either band - the only scare is the feigned pecking of Spot's eyes - and the 4-9 text is a plain rescue tale.

moral.text: True friends scheme together to set each other free

video_brief.key_beat: Spot lying stiff as if dead while Swift pretends to peck at his eyes and the hunter drops the turtle to lunge for a club.

age_map.rationale: Only the 9+ band exists. A war between two kingdoms ends with the crows tricking their way into the owls' single-gated cave and burning it, so that every owl dies inside; calculated betrayal and a whole host destroyed need a 9-year-old reader, and the long five-counsellor frame keeps it within 12.

moral.text: Never trust an enemy, however friendly they may seem.

video_brief.key_beat: the crows raining firebrands onto the woodpile at the cave gate while the owls, blind in the sunlight, cannot find their way out

stories.title: How the Birds Picked a King

age_map.rationale: The adapted text carries no violence - the crow only argues the owl is ugly and that two kings spell chaos - so the 4-9 band can be served even though the source kills the owl.

moral.text: One good leader is worth more than two quarrelling ones

video_brief.key_beat: The crow landing mid-ceremony, wings spread, as the anointed owl waits on the flower-strewn throne.

stories.title: How the Rabbit Fooled the Elephant

age_map.rationale: The 9+ band says the elephants killed rabbits (the rabbits 'lost many of their family members'), but the 4-9 telling softens it to 'hurt' with no on-page death, so the gentle band can be served young.

moral.text: A small clever creature can defeat a giant by outwitting it, but pretending to be what you are not is a risky game.

video_brief.key_beat: Victory the rabbit perched on a rock-pile, declaring himself the Moon's envoy to the towering elephant-king Four-Tusk.

age_map.rationale: The cat eats both the partridge and Speedy on-page in the 4-9 band, so it is not a 4-5 story.

moral.text: A corrupt judge destroys the very creatures who trusted him.

video_brief.key_beat: The holy-seeming cat Curd-Ear pouncing and seizing the partridge and Speedy in his paws and teeth.

age_map.rationale: The three rogues eat the goat in both bands, and the trick relies on repeated deception a child must track across three encounters.

moral.text: Do not let strangers' repeated lies make you doubt what you plainly see.

video_brief.key_beat: The Brahman flinging the goat to the ground and bolting home while the three rogues close in on their prize.

age_map.rationale: Haughty is stung to death by the ants on-page in both bands, so it is not a 4-5 story.

moral.text: Pride and a shortcut destroy even the strongest when a united crowd turns on them.

video_brief.key_beat: The wounded black snake Haughty buried under a seething, stinging mass of ants.

age_map.rationale: The son is bitten by the snake and dies on-page in both bands, a child death that pushes the floor to 7.

moral.text: Greed for more turns a daily gift into a death sentence.

video_brief.key_beat: The snake's hood flashing out of the anthill as its fangs strike the greedy boy.

age_map.rationale: The king orders his club-carrying soldiers to kill all the swans in both bands; the birds escape, but the command to slaughter drives the floor up.

moral.text: A king who overreacts to a petty quarrel loses the loyal creatures who served him.

video_brief.key_beat: The flock of golden swans bursting into the sky as the soldiers' clubs swing over an empty shore.

age_map.rationale: Only a 9+ band exists and it carries misogynist framing ('a wife's love... for her husband') plus the dove's self-sacrifice and two characters entering the funeral fire to die and rise to heaven.

moral.text: True devotion proves itself in sacrificing oneself for another.

video_brief.key_beat: The dove ascending to heaven as his grieving wife follows him into the flames and becomes radiant.

stories.title: The Old Man with the Young Wife

age_map.rationale: Curation flags murder x2, and the core is an unhappy arranged marriage (a young wife who shuns the old merchant in bed), so it is not a 4-6 story despite the tame 4-9 telling.

moral.text: Even an apparent enemy can become a benefactor when met with kindness.

video_brief.key_beat: The terrified young wife suddenly clinging to old Lovelorn as the thief slips into the dark bedchamber.

stories.title: The Snake in the Prince's Belly

age_map.rationale: A snake lodged in the prince's belly makes him ill and two squabbling snakes are driven out with mustard and hot water; the 4-9 text carries no death, just mild threat and a cure.

moral.text: Quick wit and listening can cure what strength cannot

video_brief.key_beat: The snake's head poking from the sleeping prince's mouth while a second snake slides out of the ant-hill and the two glare at each other.

age_map.rationale: A wife invites her lover while the husband hides under the bed, then invents a goddess's blessing to explain it - adult marital deception and a fooled husband.

moral.text: Do not reward and believe the one who clearly wronged you

video_brief.key_beat: The carpenter dancing through the village with the disgraced lover perched on his shoulder.

age_map.rationale: A mouse transformed into a girl is offered the sun, cloud, wind and mountain as suitors before choosing a mouse and being turned back; no violence, a gentle chain of suitors.

moral.text: Be happy with what you are and where you belong

video_brief.key_beat: Yajnavalkya's magic turning the tiny mouse into a twelve-year-old girl in his hands.

age_map.rationale: The golden-dung bird is snared and caged over greed for its gold, then freed by a cautious counselor; the bird is caught and imprisoned but nothing dies.

moral.text: Fools rush and fools doubt, so think before you act

video_brief.key_beat: The bird's droppings hitting the ground and flashing into gold.

age_map.rationale: four characters and a 'who guessed whose fear' chain — the 4-9 adaptation still carries it, but the tracking load is the point

moral.text: Cunning without trust boomerangs on the schemer.

video_brief.key_beat: the cave echoing Rough-Claw's roar

age_map.rationale: Only the 9+ band exists; the lazy snake feeds on the frogs it carries as a ride and a Brahman boy dies from its mistaken bite - predation and death throughout.

moral.text: Beware the predator who flatters and offers to serve you

video_brief.key_beat: Water-Foot and his counselors riding in a line on the black snake's hood while frogs hop behind.

age_map.rationale: friendship vs spouse loyalty is a genuine dilemma (best M5 story in the pilot); wife's jealousy in the 4-9 text reads as marital conflict — keep for 8+

moral.text: A quick wit keeps you out of a trap — and false friends set one.

video_brief.key_beat: the monkey claiming his heart is hidden in the tree

age_map.rationale: Even the softened 4-9 text has death: the snake eats all of Theodore's relatives and then his son Theodosius, so it is served at 9+ only.

moral.text: An alliance with a stronger power will devour you in the end

video_brief.key_beat: The black snake coiled in the hole swallowing Theodore's relatives one by one.

age_map.rationale: Only the 9+ band exists; the jackal lures the donkey Flop-Ear to be mauled and killed by the injured lion, and the jackal eats its ears and heart.

moral.text: A trickster who trusts his own trick too far loses everything

video_brief.key_beat: The wounded lion springing at Flop-Ear and landing short while the terrified donkey bolts.

age_map.rationale: A potter's head scar is mistaken for a battle wound until he confesses he fell drunk on a broken pot; he loses his honors, and no one is killed.

moral.text: Honesty is the best policy, and a scar is not a character

video_brief.key_beat: The king gazing at the potter's ugly forehead scar and mistaking it for a hero's battle-wound.

stories.title: The Jackal Who Killed No Elephants

age_map.rationale: Only the 9+ band exists; the cub threatens to kill his brothers and the lioness reveals he is a jackal, a belonging/identity conflict.

moral.text: Being raised by others does not change who you truly are.

video_brief.key_beat: The wild elephant crashes into the forest and the three cubs freeze, the jackal cub baring his teeth at his lion brothers.

age_map.rationale: Death and betrayal: the wife's adultery, the Brahman pushed into a well, and the wife falling dead by the magic words, kept even in the softened 4-9 band.

moral.text: A person's true nature shows when they gain power and wealth.

video_brief.key_beat: The wife and the cripple shove the Brahman over the edge of the well while he still thinks taking them along was a good idea.

age_map.rationale: Comic shame only, husbands shaved bald and ridden like horses; no death or injury in either band, so servable young.

moral.text: Guard your words; careless speech betrays you.

video_brief.key_beat: King Joy, bridle gripped in his mouth, carries his laughing queen on his back around the palace courtyard, neighing.

age_map.rationale: The donkey is stoned, clubbed, and shot with arrows and dies; too violent for 4-5 despite the gentle telling.

moral.text: Even the cleverest disguise cannot fool everyone forever.

video_brief.key_beat: The donkey throws back its head and brays, the tiger-skin slipping, as farmers charge out of the barley with clubs and arrows.

age_map.rationale: No death or violence; the weight is the wife's adultery and her theft of her husband's money to elope, which needs a slightly older listener.

moral.text: Misfortunes come in threes; meet them wisely.

video_brief.key_beat: The rogue wades the river carrying the money and the wife's clothes, leaving her stranded and weeping alone on the empty bank.

age_map.rationale: Only the 9+ band exists; the jackal gulls tiger and leopard over a dead elephant and fights off a rival jackal with his fangs, death and layered deception throughout.

moral.text: A clever trickster can outwit his enemies but not his equals.

video_brief.key_beat: Supersmart, paws clasped and scalp dusted white, bows low to the lion, then springs aside as the leopard tears through the elephant's hide.

age_map.rationale: Spot is savaged by the other dogs (and in the 9+ band torn apart, with the monkey killing an intruder); the 4-9 band only says he was hurt badly.

moral.text: Home is best; appreciate what you have.

video_brief.key_beat: Spot creeps out of the careless housewife's kitchen stuffed with food, only to be set upon and torn by the neighborhood dogs.

age_map.rationale: The barber clubs the monks and blood flows, plus the merchant's plan to starve himself; the 9+ band adds the barber being impaled.

moral.text: Copy another's deed without understanding it and you ruin yourself.

video_brief.key_beat: The barber swings his club down at the kneeling monks, who clink into gold, as blood spatters the monastery courtyard.

age_map.rationale: The mother staves in the loyal mungoose with a water-jar and the snake is found torn to bits (bloody mouth) - flagged gore-detail x2, murder x2; only a 9+ band exists.

moral.text: Impulsive judgment can destroy the innocent who love us.

video_brief.key_beat: The mother sees the mungoose's blood-smeared muzzle and hurls the water-jar down on him before she sees the baby is safe.

age_map.rationale: The fourth quill reveals a man permanently tortured by a wheel whirling on his head (gore-detail x2, murder x1) and the treasure chain ends in torment; only a 9+ band exists.

moral.text: Common sense is worth more than scholarship or gold.

video_brief.key_beat: The fourth quill drops and uncovers a man with a great wheel spinning endlessly on his head.

age_map.rationale: The revived lion kills the three scholars (murder x1); the 4-9 band softens the telling but the friends still die, so this is not a 4-5 story.

moral.text: Common sense beats book-learning.

video_brief.key_beat: The bare lion skeleton gains skin, flesh and blood, then rises whole and lunges while the wise friend watches from the tree.

age_map.rationale: The fishermen net and carry off Hundred-Wit and Thousand-Wit - 'Thousand-Wit is dead' in the 9+ text - a death, though the 4-9 band says only 'taken away'.

moral.text: Humility and listening save more than cleverness.

video_brief.key_beat: At dawn the net comes up out of the drained pond, Hundred-Wit and Thousand-Wit thrashing inside it.

age_map.rationale: No death; Prig is only beaten with sticks and hobbled with a mortar, all played comically - mild slapstick violence, nothing flagged.

moral.text: Take a good friend's advice.

video_brief.key_beat: Prig throws back his head and brays at the moonlit cucumber bed while lanterns light up across the fields.

age_map.rationale: Slow is beaten with clubs and stones and dies after the fairy grants his extra-arms-and-head wish - a killing present even in the 4-9 text.

moral.text: Ask for what you need, not what looks nice.

video_brief.key_beat: Slow walks into town four-armed and two-headed, the crowd recoils in horror, then raises sticks and stones.

age_map.rationale: No violence or death at all - only a shattered jar and spilled barley-meal turning Seedy white; purely comic, nothing flagged.

moral.text: Don't let daydreams blind you to what is real.

video_brief.key_beat: Seedy's foot lashes out in his sleep, kicks the hanging jar, and a shower of white barley-meal covers his face.

age_map.rationale: Three deaths: the horses burn alive, the whole monkey pack is slaughtered for their fat, and the king and retinue are devoured by the man-eating fiend - murder x3.

moral.text: Greed and revenge destroy everyone caught in them.

video_brief.key_beat: The king's retinue wades into the lotus lake and the fiend surges up, swallowing them one by one.

age_map.rationale: A cannibal fiend stalks the princess and the monkey urges him to 'Eat him!'; an overheard-conversation misunderstanding drives the whole plot.

moral.text: Even the cunning can be undone by their own fear and paranoia

video_brief.key_beat: The fiend melts back into his true monstrous form and looms toward the thief still clinging to the banyan branch.

stories.title: The Fiend Who Washed His Feet

age_map.rationale: A cannibal fiend named Cruel rides a terrified Brahman's shoulders; only the 9+ band exists and the premise is a predator carrying off a man.

moral.text: Think ahead and do not trust a friendly face

video_brief.key_beat: The Brahman bolts from the lakeside while Cruel stands frozen in the water, unable to chase because of his vow.

age_map.rationale: The 4-9 band is a gentle fruit-sharing tale (Red-Face grows too fat to walk) with no death or violence, so it serves from age 4; the 9+ band adds the monkey's betrayal of the crocodile.

moral.text: Giving or trusting too much can cost you everything

video_brief.key_beat: Red-Face so fat he cannot walk, slung over Numskull's back while the last of the fruit disappears.
